fields.description:
## Context
DSO engineers planning sweeping/repetitive changes — function-signature sweeps across many call sites, import/API renames, framework upgrades, and schema/DB migrations — currently receive a plan that assumes smallest-atomic-task decomposition. The planner over-fragments the work or misses call sites and rollback safety, so missed sites and unsafe migrations surface during sprint execution instead of at plan time. This epic makes /dso:implementation-plan detect migration-style stories and plan them as an automated-sweep + manual-verification (plus rollback for DB) structure, and gives /dso:sprint a two-pass execution ordering. The planner runs both inside the DSO plugin and in consuming projects (Python/Alembic, Django, Rails, TypeScript), so detection is stack-generic.

## Success Criteria
- /dso:implementation-plan auto-classifies a story migration-class via two sub-classifiers: (a) sweep — one logical change repeats across call sites of the specifically targeted symbol/API (not surrounding boilerplate/imports/tests) above a configurable threshold (migration.call_site_threshold, with an explicit default when unset), detected via ast-grep; (b) db — the change touches schema/migration file patterns (migrations/, alembic/, db/migrate, *.migration.ts, schema.sql) regardless of call-site count. The classification and detection query are persisted as a durable migration-class marker in the plan header; classification proceeds without user confirmation. When sg is unavailable, an explicit migration-class:inconclusive marker is recorded (never silently false) and the planner does not crash.
- For each migration-class:sweep change, the dso:task-decomposer emits an automated-sweep task carrying an explicit transform descriptor (recipe rule or sg rewrite, distinct from the detection query), recipe-preferred with agent-sweep fallback, paired with a manual-verification task whose emitted done-definition requires BOTH completeness (re-run the detection query and assert zero remaining sites; un-automatable sites recorded as inline TODO(migration) markers and enumerated in an un_automatable_sites field) and semantic correctness (run the test gate over modified files — a zero detection count without a passing test gate is not complete).
- For migration-class:db changes, the plan always emits a paired rollback task and rollback-verification task; the rollback is classified safe-revert (additive) or compensating-forward (destructive — ambiguous defaults to compensating-forward and leads with a DATA LOSS RISK note); rollback-verification asserts the resulting schema state, not merely that the task ran. The rollback pair is authored in the same plan as the forward migration.
- The dso:task-decomposer emits a feature-flag rollout task only when the rollout:feature-flags-approved tag is present on the story or its parent epic (two-hop lookup via the ticket CLI). When present, it emits a flag-guarded cutover task plus a paired flag-removal cleanup task. When absent on both (including when no parent exists), no feature-flag task is emitted and the plan header records feature_flags:prohibited with reason — regardless of any feature-flag mention in the story text.
- /dso:sprint reads the persisted migration-class marker from the plan header (it does not recompute detection); for each (automated-sweep, manual-verification) pair it sets the verification task's depends_on to the sweep task and schedules the sweep in an earlier batch; absent the marker, standard ordering applies. The two-pass flow is documented in sprint/SKILL.md.
- A fixture at tests/implementation-plan/fixtures/migration-sweep/ (synthetic codebase, at least 5 call sites of a target signature, one intentionally omitted) demonstrates in-session that /dso:implementation-plan emits a migration-class marker and an automated-sweep/manual-verification pair, and that when the sweep leaves the omitted site, the verification completeness assertion exits non-zero and surfaces the missed site — while the pre-change planner (RED-phase committed baseline) produces no marker and no paired structure. Shown with captured tool output.

## Closure Checks
(none — all success criteria are verifiable within the closing sprint session)

## State Lifecycle
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |
| migration-class marker (plan header) | /dso:implementation-plan detection | final once recorded | /dso:sprint two-pass ordering; dso:task-decomposer emission | discarded with the plan; not persisted past sprint close |
| rollout:feature-flags-approved tag | user / follow-on brainstorm capture (epic 094a-6057) | boolean presence | dso:task-decomposer feature-flag gate | user via ticket untag; else persists for epic lifetime |

## Dependencies
None blocking. The rollout:feature-flags-approved tag is produced upstream — brainstorm-side capture of that approval is a follow-on (relates_to 094a-6057, out of scope here); this epic reads the tag and defaults to prohibited (safe default). Reuses the existing recipe registry/adapters, plugins/dso/scripts/sprint/translate-recipe-to-llm-task.sh, ast-grep (sg), the ticket CLI, and depends_on — all verified present.

## Approach
Add a migration-class detection branch to implementation-plan's contextual-discovery step (dual sub-classifier: ast-grep repetition threshold on the targeted symbol for sweep; migration file-pattern match for db), persist a migration-class marker, and have the dso:task-decomposer emit automated-sweep + manual-verification pairs (and rollback + rollback-verification pairs for db), with /dso:sprint consuming the marker to order sweep before verification via depends_on. Prompt wording uses affirmative gates over prohibitions, an explicit config default, a conservative rollback default, an over-trigger guard (count only the targeted symbol), and a self-contained sprint instruction with an absent-marker fallback.

## Scenario Analysis
- Assumption (critical): rollback assumed invertible — destructive schema changes have no safe inverse; addressed by safe-revert/compensating-forward classification.
- Runtime (critical): ast-grep call-site count diverges from the true set of sites (dynamic dispatch, generated/vendored code); mitigated by the re-run-query assertion plus test gate, residual risk flagged for implementation-plan stories.
- Deployment (critical): forward migration applied before the rollback is authored; addressed by same-plan rollback authoring.
- Configuration (high): rollout tag set on the epic but read only on the story; addressed by the two-hop lookup.
- Configuration (high): sg present locally but absent in CI causing plan divergence; addressed by the persisted marker and sprint consuming (not recomputing) it.
- Assumption (high): detection pattern reused as the sweep pattern; addressed by the explicit transform descriptor.
- Recorded for implementation planning: recipe-engine version mismatch (silent no-op sweep), LLM-fallback non-determinism across parallel sweep agents, missing lock-timeout guard for production schema migrations, and call-site-threshold false-positives on large non-repetitive stories.

## Cross-Epic Interactions
- /dso:implementation-plan skill — shared with 9ddd-117b, ab57-b534, 4001-7ad3, f7d5-59e4, dfa1-f9fd, 853a-c719, 94ed-f55c, c206-5acb, d63f-2c74, a8e8-0b23. Constraint: coordinate task-emission ordering, marker/comment namespaces, and authorship of the skill edits.
- Recipe system / translate-recipe-to-llm-task.sh — shared with c821-e995 (security recipes). Constraint: coordinate recipe registration/selection schema when multiple recipe-driven task types coexist.
- ast-grep / command resolution — shared with 986e-91c5 (fail-loud command policy), cf7b-86a9 (CI portability), w21-bsnz (remediation engine). Constraint: align the sg-absent degradation path with the command-resolution none sentinel.
- /dso:sprint ordering — shared with 0cf2-42b5, dso-8l5h, dso-94ya, e884-d0ad, 9679-695c. Constraint: preserve depends_on insertion points.
- Ticket CLI — shared with 1de7-50d4 (--reason to --resolution), 7510-0198 (--parent enforcement), 2007-26e6 (ID display). Constraint: emitted tasks must adopt current flags/format.

## Research Findings
- Migration or compatibility (completeness): re-run the same detection query post-sweep and assert empty; expect ~5% of sites to resist automation and mark them with TODO comments for the verifier. Sources: martinfowler.com/articles/codemods-api-refactoring.html; webflow.com/blog/codemods-and-large-scale-refactors-at-webflow. Shaped the SC2 verification definition.
- Migration or compatibility (rollback): down-migrations are dangerous for destructive changes — classify safe-revert vs compensating-forward; prefer expand-contract for multi-deploy. Sources: atlasgo.io/blog/2024/11/14/the-hard-truth-about-gitops-and-db-rollbacks; docs.gitlab.com/development/migration_style_guide. Shaped SC3.
- Migration or compatibility (ownership): the library owner ships the codemod with a post-run query assertion; verification confirms zero remaining sites and samples correctness. Sources: stevekinney.com/courses/enterprise-ui/codemods-at-scale. Shaped SC2.
